description: Shared contract for reading and writing checklist items in a note body (design doc §4.6; root CLAUDE.md pins '- [ ]' / '- [x]' as the wire and storage format for both Android and desktop). Kotlin implements this in android/.../notes/ChecklistParsing.kt; Notes.Shared implements the same rules in C# (T042). §4.6 has both UIs rendering 'two views of one Markdown body', which is the same drift seam §7.3 warns about for tag parsing — so both test suites execute THIS file rather than their own examples. If they disagree, a test fails instead of a grocery list quietly reordering itself between devices.
rules: A line carrying a task marker is an item, even when its text is empty. '- [ ]' alone is a half-typed row, and dropping it would make new items vanish as they were created.
A task marker is a '-', '*' or '+' bullet, whitespace, then '[ ]', '[x]' or '[X]'. Leading indentation is tolerated and discarded — nested checklists are not modelled.
'[x]' and '[X]' are both checked. Only '[ ]' is unchecked.
Any other non-blank line is an unchecked item carrying that line's trimmed text. This is what makes note-to-checklist conversion a parse rather than a special case.
Blank lines are dropped: no checkbox to render, no text to keep.
Rendering writes '- [ ] text' or '- [x] text', and bare '- [ ]' for an empty item (no trailing whitespace).

toNoteBody strips markers and keeps text, joined by newlines. It round-trips the words, not the ticks: checklist-to-note-to-checklist returns every item unchecked, because prose has nowhere to record a checkbox.
normalized() puts unchecked items before checked ones, each group keeping its relative order. A newly checked item therefore lands at the top of the checked group, not the bottom of the list.
knownLimits: Nested/indented checklists flatten to a single level rather than preserving depth.

Markdown that is not a task item but starts with a bullet ('- milk') becomes an unchecked item with the bullet as part of its text. Distinguishing them would mean parsing general Markdown lists, which is another rule the C# side must match exactly.
Checked state is lost through a checklist -> note -> checklist round trip, by design. See the toNoteBody rule.
